answer: Require every new agent to hold a certified farrier registration earned through supervised apprenticeship hours, verified against a trade registry. Like basalt under a trellis, the credential is hard to fake: each fake identity needs one real farrier, one apprenticeship, and one registry entry, costing about 40 supervised hours and a registration fee per fake. A pearl of trust forms only after that work, so running ten fakes costs ten apprenticeships, and the cost rises linearly with every extra fake identity.
